inspiration: Recolour as data: a spot animation (effect record) is a model id, an animation sequence, six source-to-destination colour pairs, a width and height resize, and ambient and contrast values (jagex2/config/SpotType.java, recol arrays at lines 31 and 34). One mesh gives many tinted variants with no new art. Frankendom use: one burst or spark mesh with six palette swaps per element or rarity.

Modular kits: identity kits are body-part records with their own recolour pairs and a head-part slot array (jagex2/config/IdkType.java, line 30). Cheap variety from few parts. Relevant to gear dressing (parity row 15).

Recipe sound effects: a Tone is a set of envelopes (frequency, amplitude, modulation rate and range, attack, release) plus five harmonics, each with a volume, a semitone offset and a delay, and a reverb delay and volume (jagex2/sound/Tone.java, lines 10-46 and 321-326). JagFX writes a 22050 Hz wave from up to ten tones (jagex2/sound/JagFX.java, getWave at lines 100-111). A whole sound bank is parameter data with no sample files. Relevant to combat cues (parity row 12).

Projectile as a kinematic step: move() advances position by velocity times elapsed ticks, adds a vertical acceleration term, sets facing from atan2 of the velocity, and advances a spot-animation frame on delay counts (jagex2/dash3d/ClientProj.java, lines 117-124). A bolt or arrow arc can use the same shape, with our own arc height and trail.

Low-resolution software texturing: the rasteriser generates a 128 by 128 texture table (jagex2/graphics/Pix3D.java, loops at lines 245-246). The flat, palette-limited look is the reference. Do not copy the rasteriser code.

Bitmap font as data: PixFont holds, per character, a mask, width, height, offsets and advance (jagex2/graphics/PixFont.java, field list seen by grep, not receipted). Relevant to readable 375 px HUD text.

briefs.label: Spark burst (recolour family)
briefs.why: One tiny burst mesh re-tinted six ways reads instantly at 375 px and costs one asset.
briefs.keep: one shared shape; colour pairs stored as data; per-element palette swap
briefs.change: our own star or ring silhouette; our palettes; a different timing curve (fast attack, longer tail)

briefs.label: Tonal hit ping (recipe sound)
briefs.why: A short pitch sweep with a few harmonics gives a clear hit cue with no sample file.
briefs.keep: envelope-driven pitch; three stacked harmonics with semitone offsets and small delays
briefs.change: our envelope shape; our harmonic ratios; a short noise transient on top; a different reverb tail

briefs.label: Bolt arc with gravity
briefs.why: A kinematic arc with a gravity term reads as a threat coming in at the right speed.
briefs.keep: velocity integrated per elapsed tick; a vertical acceleration term; facing from velocity
briefs.change: our arc height and curve; a trail instead of the spot-animation frames; a launch sound per weapon

briefs.label: Modular armour kit
briefs.why: Part slots with their own recolour pairs give many dressed looks from few parts.
briefs.keep: part slots; a per-part recolour pair list; a head-slot mask
briefs.change: our slot names and set (pauldron, greave, gauntlet); our ornament style; no copy of the slot numbering
